Chapter 8: Navigating Setbacks and Sustaining Momentum.
No journey of change is ever a straight line, is it? There are always going to be days when you slip back into old habits, or when progress just seems to stall out. Sometimes, outside pressures make it tough to keep moving forward. But here’s the thing—setbacks are part of the process. It’s not about avoiding them altogether, but about learning how to handle them with resilience and a little self-compassion.
Think of setbacks like potholes on a long road trip. Sure, they can be annoying and might even give you a good jolt, but they’re rarely the end of the journey. What really matters is how you respond when you hit one. Instead of seeing a slip-up as a failure, try looking at it as feedback—maybe it’s just a signal that something needs your attention or a slight adjustment.
So, what does navigating setbacks actually look like? Let me share a few strategies:
First, practice self-forgiveness. Let go of that need to be perfect. Nobody gets it right every time, and that’s totally okay.
Next, take a moment to analyze what happened. What triggered the old behavior? Was it stress, a certain situation, or maybe even a specific person? Once you know, you can think about what you might do differently next time.
Don’t forget to reach out to your support system. Sometimes, just talking things through with someone else can give you a fresh perspective and the encouragement you need.
And most importantly, recommit to the process. Use the setback as fuel to get back on track, instead of letting it drag you down.
Picture this: maybe you’re a leader who slips back into the habit of dominating meetings. Instead of beating yourself up, you pause and reflect—was it a particularly tough day? Did a certain topic or colleague set you off? With that awareness, you can plan a different approach for next time.
Now, sustaining momentum is just as important. That means celebrating your progress, no matter how small. Noticing even the tiniest improvement can boost your confidence and remind you that change really is possible. Maybe you kept up a new habit for a week, or maybe you caught yourself in the moment and responded differently just once. That’s worth recognizing!
Over time, you’ll notice that setbacks become less frequent—and less disruptive, too. The process of reflecting and adjusting starts to feel natural, and soon enough, those new behaviors will fit like second nature.
